identity.method_name: Snorkel-style programmatic weak supervision / data programming with a generative label model (Snorkel, arXiv 1711.10160)
identity.core_idea: Write several independent labelling functions (LFs), each a short rule that casts a noisy vote or abstains on every lake-year -- e.g. MNDWI water-loss threshold, NDVI vegetation-mask threshold, OpenStreetMap building intrusion into the legal buffer, GHSL built-up-area change, VIIRS nighttime-light change. Snorkel's label model (a generative graphical model fit by matrix completion) then estimates each LF's accuracy and pairwise correlation purely from the pattern of agreement and disagreement between LFs across all instances, with no ground truth at all, and outputs a probabilistic ('soft') pseudo-label per lake-year. A downstream discriminative classifier can then be trained on these probabilistic labels instead of on hand-annotated ones.
identity.official_dataset_ids: Snorkel itself is a framework, not a dataset. The labelling functions it would combine here draw on the project's own Sentinel-2-derived MNDWI/NDVI bands (no separate ID), OpenStreetMap building footprints (ODbL, no formal product ID), JRC/GHSL/P2023A/GHS_BUILT_S (Global Human Settlement Layer, 5-yearly epochs), and VIIRS Day/Night Band monthly composites (NOAA/VIIRS/DNB/MONTHLY_V1/VCMSLCFG on Earth Engine, or the equivalent EOG/NOAA CoastWatch product) -- none of which are currently ingested by the project except the first two.

fit_to_project.ground_truth_proxy_strategy: Programmatic weak supervision (named explicitly in this item). Cost: writing and debugging 5 labelling functions is a design task, not a manual-annotation task, so it removes per-example human labelling effort entirely -- but 3 of the 5 proposed LFs require newly acquiring and reprojecting data sources (GHSL, VIIRS) the project does not currently ingest onto its 20 m EPSG:32643 grid, and all 5 require careful threshold/coverage tuning to avoid an LF that never fires or fires on everything.
fit_to_project.input_required: MNDWI and NDVI: already computed from the project's existing B02/B03/B04/B08/B11 stack. OSM building footprints and lake polygon: already held (420,080 footprints, single 2026 snapshot). GHS_BUILT_S: must be newly downloaded and reprojected; only exists at 2015/2020/2025-type epochs, not annually. VIIRS DNB monthly composites: must be newly downloaded; native resolution ~500 m/pixel, must be resampled onto the 20 m grid (a resampling that manufactures apparent resolution rather than real information).
fit_to_project.viable_with_42_rows: yes, in the sense that Snorkel's label model naturally operates per-instance and the project's 42 lake-year rows are a natural instance set for it -- this is actually the best-matched item to the project's existing table structure among the C-group candidates. However, 42 instances is thin for reliably estimating even 5 LF accuracy/correlation parameters (published Snorkel applications typically fit the label model over hundreds to many thousands of instances); reframing to per-pixel LF votes inside each lake buffer would give a much larger nominal N, but those pixel votes are highly spatially autocorrelated within a lake-year, so the effective independent sample size for the label model's own parameter estimation remains closer to 42, or realistically 6 lakes, than to any per-pixel count.
fit_to_project.viable_without_ground_truth: needs-weak-labels, which is the entire premise of the item -- but critically, all five weak labels are derived from data the project already has or can script-fetch itself, so zero external human annotation effort is required at all; the 'cost' shifts entirely into labelling-function design and validation.
fit_to_project.resolution_match_20m: Mixed. MNDWI/NDVI: native match at 20 m. OSM: vector, resolution-agnostic in principle but represents a static single 2026 snapshot. GHS_BUILT_S: published at 10 m/100 m, coarser-or-comparable spatially but far coarser temporally (5-year epochs, not annual). VIIRS DNB: ~500 m/pixel is roughly 25x coarser than the project's 20 m grid and larger than most of the 6 lake buffers themselves, so a VIIRS-based LF for a lake buffer would return nearly the same value for the lake and its surrounding urban area -- effectively no usable spatial resolution at this scale.
fit_to_project.label_source_needed: None in the human-annotation sense. All 'labels' are Snorkel's own probabilistic outputs, generated entirely from the 5 rule-based LFs -- two of which (MNDWI, NDVI) are the same threshold rules already used in the project's current classical baseline.
fit_to_project.fixes_which_stated_limitation: Directly and explicitly targets (3) no real ground truth -- this is, per the task brief, 'the concrete published path from zero labels to trainable'. Does not fix (1) the 42-row limit (if anything, needs more effective rows than 42 to estimate the label model well). Does not fix (2) the OpenStreetMap single-snapshot problem (in fact adds a second static-snapshot layer, GHSL's 5-year epochs, compounding rather than resolving the temporal-granularity concern). Does not fix (4) the dry-season-only annual scene.
fit_to_project.handles_desilting_confound: No, and arguably makes the confound structurally worse. A desilting drawdown (Bellandur 15.7 ha in 2019 to 0.4 ha in 2021) flips the MNDWI LF, and can also flip the NDVI LF if hyacinth or bare sediment appears, and would likely show up in a GHSL 'built-up' misclassification of exposed lakebed as well -- three LFs derived, directly or indirectly, from the same optical scene would agree simultaneously on a desilting year. Because the label model infers LF reliability from agreement, this simultaneous, spurious agreement would be read as high-confidence evidence and produce a strong 'encroached' pseudo-label for a year that is in fact routine municipal maintenance.
fit_to_project.handles_hyacinth_confound: No, for the identical structural reason. A hyacinth bloom flips MNDWI (water becomes non-water) and NDVI (vegetation-positive) together; both signals originate in the same Sentinel-2 reflectance, so they are not two independent votes, they are one signal counted twice. Snorkel's default label model assumes conditional independence given the true label (see leakage_risk) and has no way to detect this collinearity on its own; Bellandur and Varthur, the two most hyacinth-affected lakes, are exactly where this failure mode is most likely to bite, and should be cross-checked against the published macrophyte-cover mapping (MDPI Remote Sensing 2020, doi 10.3390/rs12223843).
fit_to_project.legal_traceability: Only the OSM-building-intrusion LF has any cadastral flavour in principle (footprints could in theory be checked against Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority or Survey of India records), but the OSM layer used here is a single fixed 2026 snapshot with no legal status of its own, so the LF itself carries no legal traceability either. None of MNDWI, NDVI, GHSL or VIIRS reference any cadastral or legal boundary. At the 20 m pixel scale, both the 30 m Supreme-Court-reinstated buffer and the 75 m former NGT buffer are only 1-4 pixels wide, so a Snorkel probabilistic label built from pixel-level LF votes inside that buffer is too spatially coarse to support a buffer-specific legal claim; at best it supports a qualitative, lake-wide statement.
fit_to_project.temporal_granularity: Checked per-LF, as required. MNDWI, NDVI: genuinely vary year to year -- real signal. OSM building intrusion: fixed 2026 snapshot, zero within-lake temporal variance across all 7 study years -- the exact flaw already flagged in the project's own building_data constraint, now imported as a labelling function rather than fixed. GHSL built-up change: sampled only every 5 years (2015/2020/2025-type epochs); within the 2019-2025 study window this yields at most 2 genuine observations, with 2019 and 2021-2024 requiring nearest-epoch fill or interpolation -- largely static across multi-year spans. VIIRS nighttime lights: monthly composites do vary month to month and year to year in principle, giving genuine temporal signal, but at ~500 m resolution the variation reflects neighbourhood-scale urbanisation, not lake-buffer-scale encroachment -- real temporal variance at the wrong spatial scale for this project's 6 small lake buffers.

implementation.libraries: snorkel (pip install snorkel; snorkel.labeling.LabelModel, snorkel.labeling.PandasLFApplier, snorkel.labeling.LFAnalysis for coverage/conflict diagnostics); pandas for the lake-year table; geopandas/rasterio for OSM/GHSL geometry handling; Earth Engine Python API or a STAC client for VIIRS DNB and GHSL retrieval.
implementation.pretrained_weights: None needed or available. The label model is a small generative model (order of 5-10 parameters for 5 LFs) fit from scratch on the project's own LF-output matrix each run; there is no pretrained checkpoint for Snorkel's label model, and none is required. Any downstream discriminative classifier trained on the resulting soft labels is a separate modelling choice outside this item's scope.
implementation.licence: Snorkel: Apache 2.0 (github.com/snorkel-team/snorkel), fully usable academically. GHSL: public domain / CC BY 4.0 (European Commission Joint Research Centre). VIIRS DNB via NOAA: public domain (US government work). OpenStreetMap: ODbL, requires attribution and share-alike for derived data products, fine for an academic project with attribution.
implementation.compute_requirement: Trivial for the label model itself: fitting Snorkel's LabelModel on a 42-row x 5-LF matrix is a sub-second CPU operation, and even a per-pixel-reframed matrix (tens of millions of rows) fits comfortably in laptop RAM and CPU time. The real cost is data engineering -- downloading, reprojecting and epoch-aligning GHSL and VIIRS onto the 20 m grid -- which is I/O- and bookkeeping-bound, not compute-bound. No GPU or Colab/Kaggle GPU quota is needed at all for this item.
implementation.student_days: 2-3 days to wire up the 3 already-available LFs (MNDWI, NDVI, OSM), since their thresholds already exist in the current baseline. 4-6 days to acquire, reproject and epoch-align GHSL and VIIRS and turn them into usable LFs, the dominant cost. 2-3 days to fit and diagnose the Snorkel LabelModel (coverage/overlap/conflict analysis, correlation checks) and write up the circularity caveat honestly. Total realistically 8-12 student-days, most of it new-data acquisition rather than modelling.

evaluation.metrics: Snorkel's own ground-truth-free diagnostics first: LF coverage (fraction of lake-years each LF votes on), overlap and conflict rates (snorkel.labeling.LFAnalysis). Then agreement between the resulting probabilistic label and the existing MNDWI/NDVI classical baseline (expected to be high, since 2 of 5 LFs are essentially that baseline) and, as a face-validity spot-check only, agreement with the handful of documented court/news cases from item C4 -- not a formal test set. Ordinary accuracy/F1 cannot be computed at all, since there is no ground truth to score against.
evaluation.validation_protocol: leave-one-lake-out for any diagnostic that treats lakes as exchangeable units. With only 6 lakes, and the label model needing pooled agreement statistics across all instances to estimate LF accuracies, holding out an entire lake starves the already-thin 42-row fit of a meaningful share of its signal; the more defensible compromise is to fit the label model once, unsupervised, on all 42 rows (there is no train/test leakage in the classical sense at this stage, since no ground truth is being fit), and reserve leave-one-lake-out strictly for any downstream discriminative classifier trained afterward on the resulting soft labels.
evaluation.leakage_risk: This is the item's central, explicitly disclosed risk, and it maps directly onto the task's circularity objection. If several LFs are computed from the same Sentinel-2 scene (MNDWI and NDVI are both near-linear functions of the same B03/B04/B08/B11 reflectance, and GHSL's built-up classification is itself partly derived from similar optical composites), then 'agreement between LFs' is not independent corroborating evidence -- it is the same underlying pixel values counted more than once through different formulas. Snorkel's label model infers LF reliability from inter-LF agreement, so correlated LFs get systematically over-weighted: the original Snorkel paper's own worked example shows that 5 correlated 50%-accurate LFs mixed with 5 independent 99%-accurate LFs get mis-estimated as 100% and 50% accurate respectively when independence is wrongly assumed. Here the imbalance is worse: potentially 3 of 5 LFs (MNDWI, NDVI, GHSL) share one underlying optical source, versus at most 2 (OSM, VIIRS) with a genuinely distinct sensing modality, and even those two are static or too-coarse (see temporal_granularity).
evaluation.uncertainty_reporting: A genuine, disclosed advantage of this item: Snorkel's LabelModel outputs a true per-instance probability, not a bare point estimate, which is a real uncertainty signal that most other C-group items lack by default. However, the model's own training-time parameter estimates (LF accuracy, correlation) carry no confidence interval, and with only 42 rows and 5 LFs those estimates are themselves high-variance; this should be bootstrapped across a lake-year resample (or a leave-one-lake-out refit) before being trusted or reported as stable.
evaluation.augmentation_honesty_risk: Not applicable in the SMOTE/GAN/diffusion sense -- no synthetic examples are generated. A structurally similar risk applies and must be disclosed the same way: the label model can manufacture the appearance of 'several independent lines of evidence converging' (MNDWI + NDVI + GHSL all agreeing) when in fact it is one optical signal passed through near-collinear formulas, laundering a single threshold into a probability. Any panel-facing presentation of a 'high-confidence' Snorkel label must disclose this as a reweighting of correlated proxies, not independent corroboration.

evidence.published_performance: Snorkel (arXiv 1711.10160, VLDB 2018): across 6 benchmark tasks (predominantly text/relation-extraction, one radiology-image triage task), the learned generative label model with LF-correlation modelling improved F1 by a mean of 5.81 points and up to 132% relative over unweighted majority vote of the same LFs [verify -- figures from the paper's own benchmarks, not independently reproduced]; none of these 6 tasks are remote sensing. Weakly Supervised Ephemeral Gully Detection (arXiv 2511.13891, 2025) is the closest confirmed application of a Snorkel-style generative label model to a remote-sensing land-surface-process detection task, combining Vision-Language-Model-derived weak labels over >18,000 high-resolution images collected across 13 years of US agricultural fields, with the weakly-supervised student model reported to outperform both the raw VLM labels and the label model alone [specific accuracy/F1 figures and confirmation that the exact Snorkel LabelModel formulation, rather than a Snorkel-inspired variant, was used could not be fully verified in this research pass, verify].
evidence.study_area_of_that_work: Snorkel's own benchmarks: general NLP, biomedical text and one clinical-imaging task, no geospatial component. The gully-detection paper: US agricultural fields, soil/plant-science-labelled ground locations -- not India, not lakes or wetlands, and not Sentinel-2.
evidence.applies_to_indian_urban_lakes: No. No confirmed application of Snorkel-style weak supervision to Indian urban lakes, Bengaluru, or any wetland-encroachment task was found in this research.
evidence.evidence_recency: Snorkel's foundational paper is 2017/2018 (arXiv 1711.10160), pre-2020 and flagged accordingly, though it remains the actively maintained reference implementation (github.com/snorkel-team/snorkel, with follow-on work such as Snorkel MeTaL and Varma et al. 2019 on learning LF dependency structure). The closest remote-sensing analogue found, the ephemeral-gully detection paper, is 2025 (arXiv 2511.13891), within the required post-2020 window.
evidence.primary_sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.10160 ; https://snorkel.readthedocs.io/en/v0.9.3/packages/_autosummary/labeling/snorkel.labeling.LabelModel.html ; https://github.com/snorkel-team/snorkel ; https://github.com/HazyResearch/metal (Snorkel MeTaL, dependency-aware label model) ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.13891 (Weakly Supervised Ephemeral Gully Detection, closest remote-sensing analogue) ; GHSL P2023A documentation: https://ghsl.jrc.ec.europa.eu/ ; VIIRS DNB via NOAA/EOG: https://eogdata.mines.edu/products/vnl/ ; OpenStreetMap ODbL licence: https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright ; macrophyte cross-check: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs12223843.

risk.failure_modes: (1) Conditional-independence violation: 3 of 5 LFs (MNDWI, NDVI, GHSL) share the same underlying optical reflectance signal, inflating estimated LF accuracy and producing overconfident probabilistic labels exactly on desilting/hyacinth years; (2) thin data: only 42 rows (6 lakes) to estimate even a handful of LF accuracy/correlation parameters reliably, well below the hundreds-to-thousands of instances typical in published Snorkel applications; (3) low real information from 2 of 5 LFs: GHSL's 5-year cadence and VIIRS's ~500 m resolution contribute little genuine signal at this study's annual, sub-lake scale, effectively reducing '5 labelling functions' to closer to 2-3 independently informative signals; (4) circularity: because 2 of the 5 LFs are literally the project's existing classical baseline thresholds, a 'high-confidence' Snorkel label mostly restates 'MNDWI and NDVI already agreed', adding a probabilistic wrapper rather than new information over the current_method this project is meant to beat or justify replacing.
risk.panel_defensibility: A panel will ask directly: 'if you wrote all five labelling functions from data ultimately derived from the same Sentinel-2 scene and two static/coarse auxiliary layers, what did combining them actually add?' The honest answer is a formal probabilistic reweighting of a handful of correlated proxy rules, not new independent information, unless GHSL and VIIRS can be shown to contribute appreciably and independently at this study's spatial/temporal scale -- which the resolution and temporal analysis above indicates they mostly do not. This is a specific, answerable objection, and the method survives scrutiny only if presented exactly this way: as a disclosed reweighting of correlated weak signals, never as manufactured independent evidence.
risk.honest_expectation: Realistically, the Snorkel label model's soft output will closely track the existing MNDWI/NDVI classical baseline, since those two LFs (or close relatives) dominate the vote, with GHSL and VIIRS contributing marginally given their epoch/resolution mismatches at this scale. The legitimately reportable deliverable is a probabilistic reweighting of the project's existing weak rules, useful as a soft confidence score for a downstream classifier or for flagging lake-years worth closer manual review -- but it does not manufacture a genuinely new, ground-truth-quality encroachment signal, and the circularity caveat must be disclosed prominently rather than presented as validation.

verdict.recommended_rank: consider-with-reasons -- the most standard, citable, genuinely 'zero-labels-to-trainable' published route among this project's candidate answers to the missing-ground-truth problem, and cheap to implement since 2-3 of 5 LFs already exist as the current baseline, but only if the write-up explicitly discloses that most LFs are correlated derivatives of the same Sentinel-2 scene and that GHSL/VIIRS add little independent signal at this resolution and scale; reject as a way to manufacture new ground truth or to claim independent multi-source corroboration.
verdict.one_line_for_the_guide: We implemented Snorkel's generative label model over five labelling functions (MNDWI, NDVI, OSM building intrusion, GHSL, VIIRS) to turn our existing rules into soft probabilistic pseudo-labels, but we disclose that most of these functions are correlated derivatives of the same Sentinel-2 scene, so the result is a principled reweighting of our existing weak rules, not independently validated ground truth.
